clue.text: Rare skin condition is so itchy, nasty, involving hospital

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so one piece is wrapped inside the other
something nasty is twisted out of its nice form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A patient with a rare complaint is so itchy that a hospital visit is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is the clue's own description of the symptom, which makes the clue nearly &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichthyosis is a genetic disorder that leaves the skin dry and scaly, like a fish's; it is uncommon.

clue.text: Composer's wife maybe wearing coloured bands in black stuff

parts.note: Clara Schumann, pianist wife of the composer Robert Schumann
you are 'in' clothes you are wearing

explanation.surface: A composer's wife wears a striped dress inside some dark material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like a container signal but simply supplies IN; the black stuff is coal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarain is the name for the bright, glossy layers seen in banded coal, so it is a band type within coal.

clue.text: Work during strike producing call to buzz off? (5, two words)

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to strike is to hit
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone working through an industrial strike is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'strike' reads as industrial action but is a blow; HOP IT is British slang for 'go away'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Hop it!' is an informal British command telling someone to leave at once, the same as 'buzz off'.

clue.text: Marsupial one's kept in barrel

indicators.note: what is kept in something is held inside it

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
a means one

explanation.surface: A marsupial is kept in a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuan is a small Australian brush-tailed phascogale, a pouched mammal.

clue.text: Example of arrogance I brush off

indicators.note: something off is wrong or awry, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone haughtily brushes others off, a sign of arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'brush off' someone is itself arrogant, so the surface acts out the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubris is excessive pride or presumption, the classic form of arrogance in Greek tragedy.

clue.text: 'Anatomical "viaduct"'? Joins together lecture for audience (9, two words)

indicators.note: what is for an audience is heard rather than seen, so the sound counts

parts.note: to yoke is to join together
a lecture is a talk

explanation.surface: A lecture on how things are joined is delivered to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'viaduct' is a duct: the yolk stalk links the embryo's gut to its yolk sac.
explanation.definitionFit: The yolk stalk is the narrow embryonic channel joining the midgut to the yolk sac, a duct passing nutrients.

clue.text: Source of oil? Understand money, taking in written text

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within

parts.note: to see is to understand
M is an abbreviation for money
MS is manuscript, a written text

explanation.surface: Getting the money depends on reading the written text.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion comes last: the first two pieces join into one word, which then opens up in the middle for the manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Semsem is an old variant name for sesame, whose seeds are pressed for oil.

clue.text: Re such application of flavour — could be sprinkling sugar, nice

indicators.note: sprinkled things land scattered anywhere, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these two letters, joined to the answer, make up the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook describes flavouring a dish by sprinkling on sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: RE plus the answer is an anagram of SUGAR NICE, so take RE away from that fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucing is the act of putting a sauce on food, one way of adding flavour.

clue.text: Tidal flood, as on eastern river

parts.note: e.g., for example, can mean 'as' (as in 'cities, as London')
E is the abbreviation for eastern
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tidal surge sweeps up an eastern river.
explanation.definitionFit: Eger is a variant spelling of eagre, a tidal bore: a wave of floodtide rushing upstream.

clue.text: Small intestine to penetrate in men so being operated on

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, so it sits inside
what is operated on is cut and rearranged by a surgeon, so these letters change order

parts.note: taken as written
to enter is to penetrate

explanation.surface: Surgeons cut into the small intestine of men under the knife.
explanation.definitionFit: The mesenteron is the midgut, the embryonic section of the alimentary canal from which much of the small intestine forms.

clue.text: The main idea, dull but lacking depth

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to cloud is to dull or make dim
D is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A dull idea that is lacking any depth.
explanation.definitionFit: A clou, from French for nail, is the chief point of interest or central idea on which things hang.

clue.text: E.g. TV reporting, short of introduction as surplus

indicators.note: short of its introduction means its opening letter is missing

parts.note: TV news reporting is coverage

explanation.surface: Television news, lacking an introduction, is mere filler.
explanation.definitionFit: An overage is an excess amount, a quantity left over beyond what was needed.

clue.text: What's qualified dad to appear in Telegraph?

indicators.note: appearing in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: a cable is a telegraph message
pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: Was dad qualified to appear in the Daily Telegraph newspaper?
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T suggests the newspaper; it is a verb or noun for a telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone capable is competent and fit for a task, the sense of qualified.

clue.text: Tapering bloomers: cover end of tear one got on upended stone

parts.note: a cap is a cover

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of tear
Roman numeral for one
to pan out is to get on or turn out

indicators.note: in a down clue, upended means turned upside down, so read the word bottom to top

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: Bloomers torn and covered after someone stood on an overturned stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants in British English are underwear, so 'bloomers' pulls that way; here they are trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri pants are close-fitting calf-length trousers that narrow towards the ankle.

clue.text: Expressions, oddly ugsome, concealing what's central to disgust

indicators.note: done oddly, things come out in a strange order
what is concealed is hidden from view, so it drops out of the letters

parts.note: taken as written; ugsome is an old word for loathsome
the middle letter of disgust

explanation.surface: Faces pulled at something loathsome hide a core of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Moues are pouting facial expressions, typically of distaste.

clue.text: Oily treatment for heart portion trapped in foreign river

indicators.note: something trapped in another is held inside it

parts.note: the Seine flows through Paris
a portion is a part

explanation.surface: An oily remedy for the heart is caught in a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparteine is an oily liquid alkaloid from broom, once used to regulate heart rhythm.

clue.text: Scene of siege? Richard's leader involved in one

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: a word's leader is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of Richard

explanation.surface: Richard the Lionheart leads at the scene of a crusader siege.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard I besieged Acre in 1191 on the Third Crusade, so the leader in the surface really was there.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre, a port in Israel, is famous for the long siege by crusaders in 1189-91.

clue.text: Loose jargon — listen here — among Irishmen

indicators.note: what is among others sits in their midst

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish name
oi is a call for attention, like 'listen here!'

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for attention amid the loose talk of a group of Irishmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Patois is a regional dialect or the informal argot of a group, a non-standard speech.

clue.text: Monstrous pile in progress? I'll go to making it

indicators.note: the letter I is told to go somewhere else, a shift within the letters

parts.note: taken as written
something in progress is on

explanation.surface: A huge heap is still being built, and someone volunteers to finish it.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the I moves, two places along, in PILE ON. The giants of Greek myth piled Pelion on Ossa to reach heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Pelion in Greece was heaped by giants on Mount Ossa, giving the phrase for adding difficulty upon difficulty.

clue.text: Clubs featuring stars under canvas?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
astral means of the stars

explanation.surface: Golf clubs with star players camp out in tents.
explanation.definitionFit: Castral means relating to a camp, and camping is living in tents of canvas.

clue.text: Bar, worsted inside, is French

indicators.note: something inside goes within the other piece

parts.note: est is French for is
tamine is a thin worsted cloth

explanation.surface: A bar's worsted interior is French in style.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French café or bar where drinks are served.

clue.text: Honorary fellows showing fancy tie round club

indicators.note: going round something encloses it
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are worked into another form

parts.note: taken as written
a meri is a Maori war club

explanation.surface: Honorary fellows wear a fancy club tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are retired professors who keep their title as an honour.

clue.text: To the extent that, losing power, Spain's Rafa gets walloped (9, four words)

indicators.note: something walloped is battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
what is lost is no longer there, so one letter goes

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spain's tennis star Rafa Nadal loses power and gets beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Inasfar as' is a conjunction meaning to the degree or extent that something is true.

clue.text: Island group: what'll be paid for ferry circling ring?

indicators.note: circling something goes all round it

parts.note: a fare is the price of a crossing
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Ferry fares to an island group, with a ring road.
explanation.definitionFit: The Faroes are an archipelago in the North Atlantic between Iceland and Shetland.

clue.text: A suit looks odd on new friar

indicators.note: if it looks odd, it is out of its usual order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A newly arrived friar looks odd wearing a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin is short for Augustinian, a friar of the order following St Augustine's rule.

clue.text: SI unit indicating pressure on a graduated measure mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
taken as written
a scale is a graduated measure

explanation.surface: An SI unit shows the pressure on a graduated gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'SI unit indicating pressure' reads as the definition, and the pascal is indeed the unit of pressure, but 'pressure' also gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: The pascal is the International System unit of pressure, one newton per square metre.

clue.text: Old Scottish coin to issue with former monarch on

parts.note: to turn out is to issue or produce
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An old Scottish coin is issued bearing a former monarch's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The turner was a copper twopenny piece minted in Scotland in the 17th century.

clue.text: One calling from Canada shortly?

parts.note: Canada is in the north of the American continent
the abbreviation N. Amer., North America, is a short form for Canada's home

explanation.surface: Someone telephoning from Canada keeps it brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A namer is one who calls something by a name, since to call is to name.

clue.text: Disturbed when recipe is lacking wine

indicators.note: with a thing lacking, the letters are left without it

parts.note: astir means stirred up or in commotion
R, from Latin recipe 'take', heads a prescription

explanation.surface: A cook is upset when the recipe for a wine sauce is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from the Piedmont town of that name.

clue.text: Last of vessels heading for north island

indicators.note: in a down clue north is the top, so the letter named moves to the head
the last letter is the one that moves

parts.note: arks are vessels

explanation.surface: The last of the boats head north for an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, a small self-governing island near Guernsey.

clue.text: Member of priestly class, m-mature

parts.note: the stammered first letter of mature
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A priest stammers that he is mature.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 'm-' supplies its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mage is a magus, one of the Persian priestly caste known as the Magi.

clue.text: US lawman, not one catching Arab with cocaine

indicators.note: catching something holds it within

parts.note: no means not one, as in 'no man'
AR is the abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: An American lawman catches an Arab carrying cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Narco is US slang for a narcotics agent, a police officer on drugs cases.

clue.text: Food factor? See one element central to 20

parts.note: V is vide, Latin for see
Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: an element is a part of something, so only some letters are used
what is central lies in the middle, so only the middle letters count

explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' only marks that a part of 20 is taken.

clue.text: Cash bagging what's awfully dear to give in part payment (7, two words)

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Wooden sandals catch middle of prehallux!

parts.note: to get is to catch

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the central letter of prehallux

explanation.surface: Wooden sandals catch the bone beside the big toe!
explanation.walkthrough: A prehallux is an extra bone at the base of the big toe, exactly where sandal straps rub.
explanation.definitionFit: Geta are Japanese wooden clogs raised on two crosspieces; the word serves for singular and plural.

clue.text: Auditor maybe is involved in relaxation of rent line

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside
a relaxation loosens things, so the letters come apart and regroup

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An accountant is involved in easing the terms of a rent agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant; it is one who hears.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor in the root sense is a hearer, and a listener-in is someone who eavesdrops or tunes in.
